title: Zephyrine and the Alibi
premise: Ines Joubert, archivist of Saint-Aubin's cathedral, receives two letters in the same hand: one confessing to a death thirty years ago inside the locked crypt, the other promising a second confession 'when the statute runs out.' As Ines cross-references parish records, he discovers the confessing voice belongs to someone who died decades ago — and that his own late mentor helped weave the alibi protecting the killer, who is now a beloved figure of the cathedral community. Racing the statute's expiration and the killer's quiet campaign to destroy the records, Ines must choose between loyalty to his found family among the clergy and the truth of a girl no one mourned. The story ends with Ines testifying as the crypt is unsealed at last, trading his place in the cathedral family for the girl's restored name.
about_author: Zephyrine Marchetti spent a decade cataloguing ecclesiastical archives in southern France before turning to fiction, where her love of marginalia and misfiled documents shapes every mystery she writes. She lives above a former sacristy with two opinionated cats and an unshakable belief that paper remembers what people forget.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Hand
chapters.summary: Ines Joubert, sorting bequests in the cathedral archive, opens twin letters postmarked the same day: a confession to a 1994 death in the locked crypt, and a promise of more to come. His hands shake; he recognizes the handwriting as his dead mentor Père Anselme's. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: unease — grief weaponized into curiosity.

chapters.title: The Girl in the Register
chapters.summary: Ines searches baptismal and burial registers for the name in the confession — Céleste Vidal — and finds pages razored out, the cuts old and deliberate. The sacristan, Madame Roux, warns him the crypt has been sealed by bishop's order since before his time. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: first dread; the archive itself has been wounded.

chapters.title: Alibis of the Faithful
chapters.summary: Ines reconstructs the night of Céleste's disappearance through old visitor logs: four people claim to have been together at a vigil, each corroborating the others. Among them, young then, are now-Bishop Ferrand and Ines's own mentor. POV: Ines, with flashback fragments. Emotional beat: betrayal's first cold taste.

chapters.title: What Anselme Kept
chapters.summary: In Ines's inherited papers he finds Anselme's private codicil: a sealed envelope labeled 'to open when the law forgets.' Inside, half a photograph and a note naming the fourth alibi-witness only by initial. Someone has been in the archive overnight. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: paranoia — the sanctuary watching back.

chapters.title: Madame Roux Remembers
chapters.summary: The elderly sacristan finally speaks: she was Céleste's aunt, silenced thirty years ago by grief and the bishop's authority. She gives Ines Céleste's locket, hidden in plain sight among reliquaries. POV alternates: Ines, then Roux's memory chapter. Emotional beat: found family forming around shared loss.

chapters.title: The Statute's Long Shadow
chapters.summary: A canon lawyer friend confirms the prosecution window closes in eleven days. That night the archive suffers a small fire, 'electrical,' destroying the 1994 visitor log. Ines realizes the confessor isn't confessing — he's timing his own exposure, or baiting cleanup. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: rising panic, stakes made physical.

chapters.title: Vigil, Reassembled
chapters.summary: Ines tracks down the surviving alibi-witnesses. The youngest, now a hospice nurse, breaks: the four weren't together; they rotated watch over something in the crypt, and Céleste saw it. Bishop Ferrand offers Ines a promotion and a quiet transfer. POV: Ines and the nurse. Emotional beat: temptation versus resolve.

chapters.title: The Second Letter Arrives
chapters.summary: As promised, a second confession comes — written in Céleste's own hand, dated days after her supposed death. She didn't die that night; she was imprisoned in the crypt and died later, alone, while the alibi held. Ines understands the first letter was Anselme's penance, transcribing her words. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: horror transmuted into fierce purpose.

chapters.title: Unsealed
chapters.summary: Ines forces the crypt's opening with Roux, the nurse, and a notary as witness. They find Céleste's remains and, scratched into stone, the full names of all four watchers. Bishop Ferrand arrives with police — but Ines has already mailed copies everywhere. Confrontation in the dark beneath the nave. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: climax — truth spoken aloud at last.

chapters.title: A Name Restored
chapters.summary: Months later: Ferrand resigned and charged within the statute's final hours; the cathedral reburied Céleste under her own name. Ines, no longer welcome in the institution, keeps the archive as its independent custodian, Roux and the nurse beside him. He files the last letter — his own testimony — in the register. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; loyalty kept by telling the truth.
